record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does there exist a chiral polytope whose left Petrie paths are polygons but whose right Petrie paths are not polygons?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 Is there a chiral polytope whose left Petrie paths are polygons, but whose right Petrie paths are not?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) are ranked, satisfying the standard axioms generalising the face lattice of a convex polytope: it has a least face and a greatest face, every maximal chain (flag) has the same length, it satisfies the diamond condition (between any face of rank i−1 and any face of rank i+1 incident with it there are exactly two faces of rank i), and it is strongly flag-connected. The automorphism group of an abstract polytope P acts freely on the set of flags. P is called regular if this action is transitive, and chiral if it has exactly two flag-orbits under the automorphism group such that adjacent flags always lie in different orbits.

For a chiral polytope P of rank n, fix a base flag Φ and let σ_1, …, σ_{n−1} be the distinguished generators of Aut(P) that map Φ to its i-adjacent flag's orbit representative (so σ_i changes only the face of rank i). The left Petrie motion is the automorphism σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_{n−1}, and the right Petrie motion is σ_1 σ_2^{−1} σ_3 σ_4^{−1} ⋯ (alternating). The orbits of the edges of P under the cyclic group generated by the left (respectively right) Petrie motion, traversed by following the action on edges, are called the left Petrie paths (respectively right Petrie paths) of P. Such a path is said to be a polygon when it closes up into a finite cycle without self-intersection in the appropriate combinatorial sense (i.e. it is a genuine finite polygonal closed path rather than an unbounded or improperly-closing walk).

Question: Does there exist a chiral polytope P such that every left Petrie path of P is a polygon while at least one right Petrie path of P is not a polygon?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located surveys and constructions on chiral polytopes and on left/right Petrie polygons (e.g. Coxeter's chiral 4-polytopes obtained by making left and right Petrie motions have different lengths), but no source was found explicitly resolving whether a chiral polytope can have all left Petrie paths closed as polygons while some right Petrie path fails to close as a polygon. The status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of chiral polytopes and asymmetry between left and right Petrie structures.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on chiral polytope constructions; does not resolve the asymmetric Petrie-path closure question.
